name: Astronomy on Tap: 'The Dark Night' Edition
venue: Somethin' Else at DeKalb Market Hall
why: Professional scientists and educators give themed talks on astronomy with games and cosmic trivia at a local bar.

name: Contemporaneous Ensemble: 'Seeing in the Dark'
why: Season opener featuring new music co-presented with Mantra Percussion and Recap Percussion, exploring how sound navigates darkness.

name: Sugar, We're Hoein Down: Halloween Edition Line Dancing x Emo Night
why: Halloween-themed line dancing party set to emo, alt, and pop-punk bangers; beginners welcome, steps taught on arrival.

name: The Rocky Horror Picture Show: 360 Production
why: Fully staged 360° production with shadow cast; post-show DJ sets and dance parties following the Oct 23, 24, 30, and 31 shows. Runs through Nov 1.

name: Selected Shorts: The Best American Short Stories 2026 with Viet Thanh Nguyen
why: Pulitzer Prize–winning novelist Viet Thanh Nguyen hosts a live literary performance of stories by Nathan Blum, Sigrid Nunez, and Akhil Sharma, performed by TV and stage actors.

name: Taylor Swift, 'Love Story,' and the Ancient Roman Art of Writing About Love
why: NYU classicist David Levene traces Roman elegy from ancient Rome to the Eras Tour in a lecture based on his 'It's a Love Story' course; one-hour open bar included.

name: Adam Wade: Live in New York — Storytelling Show
why: 20-time Moth Story Slam winner Adam Wade performs three to four stories from his catalog with a special guest; no two shows are the same.

name: Artists + Beers: Short Film Screening Series
why: Semi-monthly screening of short films, docs, and music videos by local filmmakers, paired with beers.

name: The Phantom of the Opera (1925) with Original Guitar and Church Organ Live Score
why: Halloween screening of the 1925 silent film classic accompanied by a newly composed live guitar and church organ score.

name: Taste of Science: 'Under Pressure: Decoding the Weather Machine'
why: Science-bar talk covering weather science from today's forecast to how AI is transforming future climate predictions.

name: Our Wicked Lady Presents: '90s Cover Band Night
why: Halloween-themed covers of Rage Against the Machine, Alice in Chains, Smashing Pumpkins, and other '90s acts.

name: The Monster High Mash: A Monster High Drag Party
why: All-Monster High-themed drag party hosted by Cheetah Quila.

name: WNYC In Conversation: Affordability Series — Second Avenue Subway Expansion
why: Live podcast taping with residents, business owners, and MTA officials discussing the long-promised Second Avenue Subway expansion and displacement tensions.

name: The Mingle Games
venue: Jaywalker at New York Distilling Co.
why: Fast-paced social games send participants from table to table meeting strangers, with cocktails, beer, and dumplings; an app lets you connect with people you click with.

name: Halloween Cover Show + Art Market
why: Live tributes to Tom Petty, the B-52s, and more, alongside an art market.

name: NYC Magic Ensemble
why: An evening of close-up magic and mentalism from the NYC Magic Ensemble at a neighborhood bar.

name: Free Outdoor Movie: Sinners at McCarren Park
why: Free outdoor screening of Sinners (2025) at McCarren Park; weather permitting.

name: MoMA PS1 School Nite: Isabella Lovestory, b0yg1rl, Ali RQ
why: PS1's new after-hours series featuring digital, internet-based, and underground acts with gallery access until 9pm; Isabella Lovestory, b0yg1rl, and DJ Ali RQ headline.

name: Goth Sk8 Halloween: Gargoyle, Llora, Nightwitch
why: Halloween goth skating party with live sets by Gargoyle, Llora, and Nightwitch; skate rental available.

name: Guillermo Del Homo: Pan's Labyrinth 20th Anniversary Drag Tribute
why: Drag tribute to Guillermo del Toro's Pan's Labyrinth on its 20th anniversary.

name: Frigid New York's Annual Days of the Dead Festival
why: Two-week festival of independent theatre and performances exploring themes of death, the afterlife, and Halloween, inspired by Día de Muertos. Runs through Nov 1.

name: 24th Annual Open House New York Weekend Festival
why: Over 300 buildings and spaces across NYC open their doors for behind-the-scenes tours, including new construction, historic landmarks, industrial spaces, and private collections.

name: Trek or Treat — Star Trek Halloween Costume Party
why: Halloween-themed Star Trek meetup and costume party with spooky space screenings, behind-the-scenes footage, and a latinum prize for best-dressed fan.

name: Tale Storytelling Show
venue: The Red Room at KGB Bar
why: Host Harmon Leon (This American Life, The New Yorker) presents an evening of NYC's best storytellers: Annie Tan, Michael Tedder, Sean O'Brien, and Michele Carlo, with music.

name: (Un)Silent Film: The General (1926)
source: The New School College of Performing Arts
why: Buster Keaton's 1926 silent classic The General with an original score by Carl Davis performed live by students from the Mannes School of Music and School of Jazz.

name: St. Kilda: One-Woman Scottish Horror Show
why: Drama League Award nominee Jody Christopherson's one-woman 'Scottish horror excursion with supernatural foley looping,' drawing on the 1930 evacuation of the Scottish archipelago St. Kilda.

name: 30th Annual Gowanus Open Studios
why: More than 400 artists, businesses, and venues in Gowanus open their doors across 90+ locations in former factories and warehouses for the neighborhood's annual studio open house. Runs Sat–Sun.

name: Brooklyn Navy Yard Annual Open House
why: Behind-the-scenes access to studios in fashion, design, and technology across the 300-acre campus, with spirits tastings, campus tours, food trucks, and live art demos.

name: Peoples' Symphony Concerts: Quatuor Danel
venue: The High School of Fashion Industries
why: French/Belgian quartet Quatuor Danel kicks off the 126th season with Beethoven, Shostakovich, and Weinberg.

name: New York Repertory Orchestra 2026–27 Season Opener
venue: The Church of St. Mary the Virgin
why: All-volunteer community orchestra opens its new season with Rachmaninoff, Rautavaara, and Martinů, featuring soprano Kendra Berentsen. Season dates: Dec 5, Feb 20, Apr 3, May 15.

name: Nü Girl Order Presents: House of Flies — Nu-Metal + Metalcore Halloween Party
why: Women-focused Halloween dance party dedicated to heavy music and horror nostalgia with nu-metal and metalcore.

name: Moving Body – Moving Image Biennial
why: Film festival of experimental, documentary, and narrative films exploring the immigrant body on camera and behind the scenes; programming and installation at Barnard through Oct 24.

name: Pigeons by the Seashore: Group Art Show
why: Group art show celebrating NYC's pigeon as urban icon, featuring work by multiple artists. On view through December.

name: Fifth Annual National Indigenous Peoples of the Americas Parade
venue: Madison Ave & E 23rd St to Broadway & 17th St
source: National Indigenous Peoples of the Americas Parade
why: Annual parade and celebration with speakers at 10am followed by the parade at noon through Flatiron.

name: Smorgasburg Diwali: Festival of Bites
venue: Marsha P. Johnson State Park (Sat) + Prospect Park (Sun)
why: Annual Diwali food festival at Smorgasburg's outdoor market locations; Saturday at Marsha P. Johnson State Park, Sunday at Prospect Park's Breeze Hill.

name: Annual Brooklyn Synth + Pedal Expo
why: Annual expo for synthesizers, effects pedals, and electronic music gear; Sat 12–6pm and Sun 10:30am–5pm.

name: Manhattan Vintage Clothing Show: Fall Edition
why: Fall edition of the vintage clothing show with dealers from across the country at Metropolitan Pavilion. Runs Fri–Mon.

name: Scaling AI Deployments
why: Founders and engineering leads from OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Fireworks, and QuantumLight discuss taking AI from early experimentation to production at scale, with firesides on deployments.

name: Zero-Human Company Hackathon by Terac at Whop HQ
why: Hackathon challenging engineers to build an autonomous agent that can run a business on its own: making decisions, handling operations, and executing with little to no human input.

name: IQT Quantum + AI 2026
why: IQT's flagship conference on the convergence of quantum computing and AI, with 80+ speakers across hardware, software, applications, and business; includes a post-quantum cryptography track on Oct 26. Runs Oct 25–27.

name: Fantasia (1940) — Handcrafted Horrors Series
why: Disney's 1940 animated classic set to Bach, Tchaikovsky, Beethoven, Stravinsky, and more, culminating in the terrifying 'Night on Bald Mountain' sequence.

name: Faust (1926) with Mont Alto Motion Picture Orchestra Score — Handcrafted Horrors
why: F.W. Murnau's 1926 German expressionist masterpiece Faust, newly restored in the original German version, with a compiled photoplay score by the Mont Alto Motion Picture Orchestra.

name: Nosferatu (35mm) with Live Musical Accompaniment by Makia Matsumura
why: 35mm screening of the 1922 horror classic Nosferatu with a live musical score performed by Makia Matsumura, part of the Handcrafted Horrors Halloween series.

name: Persona (60th Anniversary) co-presented with Newfest
why: 60th anniversary screening of Ingmar Bergman's Persona (1966), co-presented with Newfest, the NYC LGBT+ film festival.

name: MoMI Halloween Party (Members + Guests)
why: Members-only Halloween party at the Museum from 7:30–11pm with costumes encouraged.

name: MoMI Merch Meet: First Artisan Market
why: MoMI's first artisan market featuring local makers whose work celebrates the moving image — art, hats, buttons, jewelry, toys, zines, comics, and more.

name: AIA New York Common Bond 2026 Gala
why: Annual AIA NY fundraiser gala at Pier 60, celebrating honorees in support of the Center for Architecture's year-round community programs; after party 9 PM–midnight.

name: Building of the Day Tour: Melrose Library, New York Public Library
venue: Melrose Library (New York Public Library branch)
source: AIA New York / Center for Architecture
why: Archtober guided tour of the Melrose branch of the New York Public Library, examining its architecture and neighborhood context.

name: Screening: Gateways to New York — Othmar H. Ammann and His Bridges
source: AIA New York / Center for Architecture
why: Screening of Gateways to New York, a documentary on Swiss-American bridge engineer Othmar H. Ammann, who designed the George Washington, Verrazano-Narrows, and Bayonne bridges.

name: Walking Tour: Historic Buildings and New Interventions in SoHo
source: AIA New York / Center for Architecture
why: Archtober walking tour of SoHo examining the neighborhood's cast-iron historic buildings alongside contemporary architectural interventions.

name: Building of the Day Tour: Marcus Garvey Village and Extension
source: AIA New York / Center for Architecture
why: Archtober guided tour of Marcus Garvey Village, a 1970s low-rise public housing development in Brownsville by Ted Liebman, noted for its village-scale planning.

name: Walking Tour: Upper East Side Architecture Through Affluence and Ailments
source: AIA New York / Center for Architecture
why: Archtober walking tour of the Upper East Side exploring how wealth and public health shaped its 19th- and 20th-century architecture.

name: Walking Tour: Upper East Side Architecture Through Affluence and Ailments
source: AIA New York / Center for Architecture
why: Archtober walking tour of the Upper East Side exploring how wealth and public health shaped its 19th- and 20th-century architecture.

name: America's 250th Anniversary Tour of Fort Greene
venue: Fort Greene Park (meet at DeKalb Ave/Washington Park entrance)
why: Walking tour tracing Fort Greene Park's role in the American Revolutionary War, the Battle of Brooklyn, and the legacy of prison ship martyrs, led by historians Natasha Fearon and Alexandra Stevens.

name: Black History and Culture Tour of Fort Greene
venue: Fort Greene Park (meet at DeKalb Ave/Washington Park corner entrance)
why: Guided tour of Fort Greene's Black history and culture led by local historian Suzanne Spellen, covering stops from both the 'Heart of Black Fort Greene: Fulton Street' and 'Fort Greene Black History Makers and Cultural Giants' routes.

name: Fort Greene Artisans Bazaar
venue: Fort Greene Park (along DeKalb Ave between S Oxford St and Washington Park)
why: Weekly outdoor market with 30+ local designers, artisans, and makers selling upcycled fashion, handmade jewelry, small-batch apothecary, candles, accessories, and more. Every Saturday.

name: Yoga in the Park with Shala Yoga
why: Free outdoor vinyasa-style yoga class blending breath and movement; suitable for all levels, no registration required — last session of the season Oct 24.

name: Run Club with Chelsea Piers Fitness at Fort Greene Park
why: Community 3–5 mile run starting at the Fort Greene Park monument, led by Coach Skye Massey; all paces welcome. Every Tuesday through Nov 3.

name: King's County Fitness Club — Free Wednesday Workout
why: Free community-led outdoor workout every Wednesday at Fort Greene Park's Monument Plaza; all ages and abilities welcome, dogs allowed, group coffee follows.

name: Protecting Kids Online in the Age of AI — with Jonathan Haidt, Senator Kristen Gonzalez, Common Sense Media
source: Brooklyn Public Library / The TAG Movement / Reset Tech
why: 90-minute public panel on AI chatbots and youth safety, featuring social psychologist Jonathan Haidt, NY State Senator Kristen Gonzalez, and advocates from Common Sense Media; aimed at parents, teens, educators, and policymakers.

name: Black on Screen: Honoring Marlon Riggs
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
source: New York Public Library / Schomburg Center
why: Screening and tribute honoring the work of Marlon Riggs, the pioneering Black filmmaker and poet known for Tongues Untied, Ethnic Notions, and Color Adjustment.

name: Across a Crowded Room: Premiering New Musicals Made at the Library
source: New York Public Library for the Performing Arts
why: Day-long showcase of new musicals created by artists-in-residence at the Library for the Performing Arts, culminating in staged readings and songs from works-in-progress.

name: Horror Film Series: Slashers — Scream (Oct 21) and Black Christmas (Oct 28)
why: NYPL's two-part slasher film series screening iconic horror classics: Scream on Oct 21, Black Christmas on Oct 28, both at SNFL at 6 PM.

name: The Addams Family (1991) — 35th Anniversary Screening
why: 35th anniversary screening of Barry Sonnenfeld's 1991 Addams Family feature film, accompanied by related reading materials from the NYPL collection.

name: Lesia Ukrainka: The Modernist Playwright America Has Yet to Discover
why: Stage directors Virlana Tkacz and Rory Pelsue explore the fierce, psychologically charged dramas of Ukrainian modernist playwright Lesia Ukrainka — who wrestled with gender, war, desire, and power — through conversation and live readings, considering how her work might be reimagined today.

name: New Classics Film Series: Ghostbusters (1984)
source: New York Public Library for the Performing Arts
why: Halloween afternoon screening of the 1984 Ghostbusters at the Library for the Performing Arts as part of the New Classics film series.

name: The Library After Hours: Friday the 13th Edition
why: After-hours Halloween party at the iconic Schwarzman Building with dancing, live music, storytelling, classic films, and a one-night display of rare collections material exploring the evolving identity of witches.

name: Silly Old Bear! Winnie-the-Pooh at 100 — Exhibition
why: Centenary exhibition displaying original A.A. Milne mockups, E.H. Shepard illustrations, translations of the Pooh stories, and the new Roo toy gifted by Queen Camilla — plus the original stuffed toys that inspired the books. On view through Nov 30.

name: Declaring America: 1776 and Beyond — Exhibition
why: Multi-gallery exhibition at the Schwarzman Building unpacking complex, diverse stories of the American Revolution — from founding documents and protest ephemera to artworks from the Schomburg Center — through Jan 10, 2027.

name: Forging Ahead: Recent Acquisitions of Black Women Artists — Exhibition
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
source: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
why: 21 Black women artists working across media on themes of body iconography, storytelling, futurism, spirituality, and mapping Black history in a showcase of the Schomburg's recent acquisitions. On view through Mar 27, 2027.

name: Unleashed: Pets of the Performing Arts — Exhibition
source: New York Public Library for the Performing Arts
why: Exhibition drawing from the Library for the Performing Arts archives to spotlight the animals behind iconic performers — from Billie Holiday's boxer to Anna Pavlova's pet swan and Larry Kramer's hound. On view through May 8, 2027.

name: Sawyer Avenue, Sunday Afternoon — Film Screening & Panel (Cooper Union + The New Yorker)
venue: The Great Hall at Cooper Union
source: The Cooper Union / The New Yorker
why: Screening of The New Yorker Documentary's award-winning short about masked US Border Patrol agents abducting a man without warrant in Chicago, followed by a discussion with filmmaker Bill Morrison, journalist Jamie Kalven, NYCLU immigration policy strategist Devashish Basnet, and The City reporter Gwynne Hogan.

name: Praise Day for Sonia Sanchez!
venue: The Great Hall at Cooper Union
source: The Cooper Union / Gardiner Foundation Great Hall Forum
why: Celebration of poet Sonia Sanchez featuring Sweet Honey in the Rock®, Tracy K. Smith, Danez Smith, Jessica Care Moore, Ursula Rucker, Yolanda Wisher, and special appearances by Cornelius Eady, LaTasha N. Nevada Diggs, and others.

name: Aaron Gilbert: Alex Katz Chair in Painting Artist Talk
venue: Frederick P. Rose Auditorium, Cooper Union
why: Brooklyn-based painter Aaron Gilbert discusses his work depicting scenes from private everyday life under the weight of institutional forces and late-stage technocapitalism.

name: Public Art Fund Talk: Genesis Belanger
venue: Civic Projects Lab at 41 Cooper Square
source: Public Art Fund / The Cooper Union
why: Artist Genesis Belanger and Public Art Fund curator Melanie Kress discuss Belanger's sculptural installations in City Hall Park — pigmented cast concrete works exploring value, justice, authenticity, and artifice.

name: Native Voices Karenna — Lay Our Vibration Down: New York Premiere
venue: The Great Hall at Cooper Union
source: The Cooper Union / Gardiner Foundation Great Hall Forum
why: New York-stage premiere of two short operas — Trials and Tears and Sacajawea: Women of Many Names — by Grammy-nominated Mohawk cellist-composer Dawn Avery, with music direction by Danielle Olana Jagelski (Oneida/Red Cliff Band of Ojibwe).

name: In Pursuit of Life, Liberty, and Happiness — Brooklyn Museum Convening
why: Ahead of Election Day, a day-long convening on justice and democratic promise featuring Mona Chalabi, Sky Hopinka, Paola Ramos, and Yomaira Figueroa-Vasquez on mapping migration histories, followed by American Artist, Mary Enoch Elizabeth Baxter, Mariame Kaba, and Jackie Wang on alternatives to incarceration.

name: Beaux Arts Ball 2026: Home Sweet Home
source: The Architectural League of New York
why: Annual Architectural League costume ball themed 'Home Sweet Home.'

name: After Hours: New York City School Construction Authority
source: The Architectural League of New York
why: Behind-the-scenes visit to the NYC School Construction Authority, which designs and builds public school facilities across the city. Architectural League members only.

name: From Field to Form: Ocean Flora
price: $20 (free for League members and Parsons community)
source: The Architectural League of New York
why: Architectural League event on the use of ocean flora — seaweed and marine plants — as sustainable materials in architecture and design.

name: After Hours: INC Architecture & Design
venue: INC Architecture & Design office, downtown NYC
source: The Architectural League of New York
why: Visit to the downtown office of INC Architecture & Design, a 40-person NYC multidisciplinary studio co-founded by Adam Rolston, Drew Stuart, and Gabriel Benroth, known for high-end hospitality and residential projects. League members only.

name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden Fall Harvest Festival
why: Annual fall festival with live music, a cider and beer garden, pumpkin decorating, an afternoon parade, and a VIP bar with New York State cider and beer flights.

name: Transit Walk: Art and Design Secrets of Penn Station and Moynihan Train Hall
why: Walking tour through Penn Station's hidden Beaux-Arts architectural remnants and new public artworks extending into Moynihan Train Hall, led by Transit Museum expert guides.

name: Ready to Ride Event — New York Transit Museum
venue: New York Transit Museum, Downtown Brooklyn
why: Hands-on subway navigation workshop inside the historic decommissioned Court Street station: practice OMNY, turnstiles, route-mapping, and role-play real-world scenarios aboard an actual subway car. Developed for participants aged 13 through adults with developmental/learning disabilities or autism.

name: Fly Away Redbirds — Nostalgia Subway Ride
why: Round-trip excursion on the famed Redbird subway cars (in service 1959–2003), departing from the historic Old South Ferry station (opened 1905, closed to the public since 2017) and riding up to the Bronx.

name: Underground NYC Tour: Subway 101
why: Expert-guided subway tour visiting stations old and new, exploring architecture, public art, and exclusive archival images from the Transit Museum's collection.

name: Subway Swing: A Boogie for the Ages
venue: New York Transit Museum, Downtown Brooklyn
why: After-hours swing dance party inside a 1936 decommissioned subway station with live jazz bands, the hottest swing dancing, and vintage outfits — one drink ticket included.

name: Transit Walk: Second Avenue's Art and Transit History
venue: East Side of Manhattan (Second Avenue corridor)
why: Walking tour exploring Second Avenue's transit development and art collection: see an original trolley kiosk on the Queensboro Bridge, discover site-specific artworks by Jean Shin, Vik Muniz, and Sarah Sze in the Q train stations.

name: Greenbelt Adult Hike — Paulo's Peak
venue: Greenbelt Nature Center, Blood Root Valley
why: Urban Park Rangers-led adult hike through Staten Island's Greenbelt, one of New York City's largest contiguous natural areas, to Paulo's Peak.

name: Revolutionary Women — Final Week (Exhibition)
venue: New-York Historical Society, Joyce B. Cowin Women's History Gallery
why: Final week of an exhibition on how women shaped the American Revolution and lived through seven years of British occupation in New York — part of the nation's 250th anniversary celebrations. Closes Oct 25.

name: New York Hysterical: The Big History Show
why: Host Tom Delgado brings his downtown comedy show to the Upper West Side for a night of stand-up, trivia, and NYC history, with guest Jonathan Mahler (New York Times journalist and author of The Gods of New York: 1986–1990).

name: Miracle on East 4th Street: Tales from WOW Café Theatre
why: Women's History Salon celebrating WOW Café Theatre — from staging the first Women's One World Festival in 1980 to finding a permanent home on the Lower East Side — with theater artists Babs Davy, Peggy Shaw, Carmelita Tropicana, and Lois Weaver.

name: Primary Source: Manumission and Legal Freedom
why: Historian Sarah Gronningsater and curator Anne Garner discuss how antislavery lawyers and enslaved people in the late 1700s–early 1800s used a medieval writ across Northern courts to gain freedom, drawing on the Patricia D. Klingenstein Library's archives.

name: Accessible Community, Culture & Technology Fair
why: All-day event at SNFL for people who are blind, have low vision, or live with other disabilities: live demos of the latest adaptive technology, a keynote panel, and organizations working in education, employment, and advocacy. Open to all.

name: Pre-Halloween Last Friday at the Schomburg Center
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
price: Free (rush entry — advance tickets sold out)
source: New York Public Library / Schomburg Center
why: Spooky Last Friday Halloween party at the Schomburg Center with music by DJ Shug, dancing, drinks, and good vibes. Free entry tickets are sold out; rush entry available at the door.

name: The City Speaks: An Interactive One-Man Show of New York Slang & Speech
venue: Henry Street Settlement, Lower East Side
why: Debut performance of an interactive one-man theatrical experience inside the historic Henry Street Settlement, exploring the evolution of New York City's slang and speech.

name: Exclusive Truffle Pasta Making Experience @ The Urbani Truffle Lab NYC
why: Hands-on truffle pasta making workshop at the Urbani Truffle Lab, guided by truffle experts.

name: Exclusive Tour Inside the Woolworth Building: NYC's Cathedral of Commerce
why: Behind-the-scenes tour inside the Woolworth Building, the 1913 skyscraper known as the 'Cathedral of Commerce,' including access to areas closed to the public.

name: Grave Robbers of New York: Exploring the City's Body Snatching History
why: Halloween-appropriate walking tour exploring New York City's dark history of body snatching, grave robbing, and the city's role in 19th-century medical anatomy supply chains.

name: The NYC Medieval Armored Combat Experience
why: Hands-on medieval armored combat experience in New York City — don actual armor and learn historic fighting techniques.

name: The Secret Eats of Chinatown: Manhattan Food Crawl
why: Guided food crawl through hidden spots in Manhattan's Chinatown, exploring hole-in-the-wall restaurants and vendors that locals frequent.

name: Secrets of the East River: NYC's Hidden Infrastructure by Ferry
why: Ferry-based tour revealing NYC's hidden East River infrastructure — bridges, power plants, water tunnels, and industrial history visible from the water.

name: Exclusive Trip Inside the Loew's Valencia: NYC's First 'Wonder Theatre'
why: Exclusive access inside the Loew's Valencia, one of NYC's five atmospheric 'Wonder Theatres' (1929) in Jamaica, Queens — rarely accessible to the public.

name: After-Hours Conservation Lab Tour @ The New York Historical
why: After-hours behind-the-scenes tour of the New-York Historical's conservation lab, where staff preserve and restore artifacts from the museum's extensive collection.

name: 2026 Louis Auchincloss Prize Honoring Colson Whitehead
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Presentation of the Louis Auchincloss Prize to two-time Pulitzer Prize winner Colson Whitehead, in a moderated conversation with New York Times critic Wesley Morris. The prize celebrates writers and artists whose work illuminates the five boroughs.

name: First Responders Appreciation Night: Free Late-Night Wednesday
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: MCNY opens its doors free for an evening honoring New York's first responders during National First Responders Day month. Part of the museum's Free Late-Night Wednesdays series. Open to all.

name: Halloween Bash: Ghosts of New York
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: MCNY's annual Halloween Bash with costume theme 'Ghost of a Famous New Yorker': live tribute and drag performances by Mango, Tyrese Allums, Purss'ophonie & Corma Kelly, costume contests, themed cocktails at the Park View Bar, and DJ Misbehaviour sets on the South Terrace.

name: Interintellect Festival: GenZ's Economics and Culture
why: In-person NYC festival exploring how Gen Z is rethinking work, faith, and success, with AI economist Rohit Krishnan, economist Allison Schrager, playwright Matthew Gasda, progress author Abi Olvera, and political columnist Shadi Hamid.

name: From Field to Form: Ocean Flora — Using Marine Materials in Architecture
venue: The Architectural League of New York
why: Panel of ocean farmers, marine-material manufacturers, and architects discusses building with sargassum blocks, eelgrass insulation, and kelp biocomposites — how to learn from, repair, and build with the world's oceans. Panelists include a Tecnológico de Monterrey professor, Seaweed City co-founder, and Danish eelgrass-product maker Søuld. Moderated by Yale's Mae-ling Lokko.

name: Performance: What Season Is It, America?
why: A performance work running the full week as part of the Drawing America: US@250 finale series at the Brooklyn Museum — five days of live art in the galleries exploring American identity and the current moment.

name: Sculpting the (Un)Spoken: Participatory Performance with Iris van Herpen
why: Participatory performance over three days in the Iris van Herpen exhibition galleries — a weekend-long immersive event with the visionary Dutch designer whose couture blurs science, nature, and fashion.

name: Birdwatching Walk with Author Julia Rothman (Bird Anatomy)
why: Morning birdwatching walk in Prospect Park with author Julia Rothman celebrating her illustrated Bird Anatomy, led by her father Jack Rothman — highlighting both NYC bird residents and migratory visitors. Meet at Endale Arch.

name: When the Knicks Nearly Formed a Minyan: 1946 and the Genesis of Big-League Basketball in New York
why: Basketball historian Avi J. Aronsky shares Knicks lore and piquant stories about the franchise's earliest days — a deep dive into New York basketball history from 1946.

name: Bodega Cats of New York with Author Dan Rimada
why: Dan Rimada reveals the making of Bodega Cats of New York (photos by Gulce Kilkis) — how he got to know the cats and the bodega workers behind the counters. The quintessential NYC neighborhood culture book.

name: New York Times Opinion Writers Unpack the 2026 Midterm Elections
venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Central Library, Dweck Center
why: Live taping of The Opinions podcast with NYT columnists Michelle Cottle, David French, and Jamelle Bouie breaking down the 2026 midterm results and their implications for the next two years. Audience Q&A included.

name: The Sun Also Rises at 100 — Anniversary Reading with Maya Hawke, Sarah Pidgeon, Richard Schiff, Jay McInerney
why: Centennial celebration of Hemingway's The Sun Also Rises, with a special anniversary reading featuring Maya Hawke, Sarah Pidgeon, Richard Schiff, and Jay McInerney bringing the characters to life 100 years later — one of the year's most starry literary events.

name: Maira Kalman: Joy
why: Beloved NYC artist and author Maira Kalman in conversation about Joy, exploring creativity, delight, and the ideas behind her latest illustrated work.

name: Annie Proulx: New and Collected Stories (with Michael Cunningham)
why: Pulitzer Prize-winning author Annie Proulx discusses her new and collected stories in conversation with Michael Cunningham — two Pulitzer Prize winners in conversation at 92NY.

name: Jen Percy & E. Jean Carroll: Girls Play Dead (with Jessica Bennett)
why: Jen Percy and E. Jean Carroll in conversation with journalist Jessica Bennett around Girls Play Dead — a charged discussion between two writers who have examined violence, gender, and survival.

name: Sinister Scents and Perfumed Potions
why: Hands-on perfume-making class with a Halloween bent — create spooky-season scents and potions. The Brainery's signature affordable, accessible small-group format.

name: Haunted History: The Age of the Witch Hunts
why: A history lecture/discussion exploring the real social, religious, and political forces behind the witch hunt era — just in time for Halloween. Brooklyn Brainery's intellectually curious format.
